body.statement:
On the simultaneous active event of \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}native\mbox{-}active\mbox{-}resolvent}\), the exact scalar equations for the native fill and reported rank projection admit the uniform expansion
\[
 \widehat M_{it}-M_{it}
 =\ell_{it}(R_{it}\epsilon)
  +q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)
  +r^{(3)}_{it}+r^{(\mathrm{pol})}_{it}+r^{(\mathrm{res})}_{it}.
\]
Here \(r^{(3)}_{it}\) is the integral third-and-higher projection remainder, \(r^{(\mathrm{pol})}_{it}\) is the polar-factor and regularization remainder after cancellation of the order-\(\lambda\) shrinkage term, and \(r^{(\mathrm{res})}_{it}\) is the scalar-resolvent substitution remainder. Uniformly on the same event,
\[
 \|D^2\mathcal P_r(M^{it})\|\le C\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^{-1},
 \qquad
 \|D^3\mathcal P_r(M^{it})\|\le C\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^{-2},
\]
and the linear and quadratic terms are exactly the declared \(\ell_{it}\) and \(q_{it}\), including the negative donor--pre overlap in \(\ell_{it}\).
body.proof_tex:
Retain the local notation of the preceding lemma and write \(x=M_{0,k}+\delta\), \(Z(x)=M_0+E+\delta e\), \(S(Z)=\mathsf S_r(Z)\), and \(p(Z)=[\mathcal P_r(Z)]_k\). On the active event, the two exact equations are
\[
 x=p\{Z(x)\}-\lambda S\{Z(x)\}_k,
 \qquad \widehat M_{it}=p\{Z(x)\}.
\tag{15}
\]
They must be expanded jointly; expanding only the second equation would retain a spurious shrinkage term.

For completeness, derivative bounds follow from a resolvent calculation. Apply the symmetric dilation
\[
 \mathcal A(Z)=\begin{pmatrix}0&Z\\ Z^{\top}&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
and surround its \(2r\) nonzero signal eigenvalues by disjoint contours at distance \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/4\) from zero. Differentiating
\[
 \Pi(Z)=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_{\mathcal C}
 (zI-\mathcal A(Z))^{-1}\,dz
\]
twice and three times, and multiplying the resulting singular-space projectors by \(Z\), gives
\[
 \|D^2\mathcal P_r(M_0)[A,B]\|_F
 \le \frac C{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}\|A\|_F\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}+(A\leftrightarrow B),
\tag{16}
\]
\[
 \|D^3\mathcal P_r(M_0)[A,B,C]\|_F
 \le \frac C{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}^2}
 \sum_{\mathrm{cyc}}\|A\|_F\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|C\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{17}
\]
The same contour calculation with coordinate projections inserted before taking norms gives the rowwise version of (16)--(17); each insertion of the target row or column contributes its local leverage square root. Equations (5)--(6) of the preceding proof therefore prevent the operator-norm loss that would arise from applying (16) to the target cell only at the end.

Put \(T=D\mathcal P_r(M_0)\), \(Q(A)=\tfrac12D^2\mathcal P_r(M_0)[A,A]\), \(h=\langle e,T(e)\rangle_F\), and \(t(E)=[T(E)]_k\). Taylor expansion of the first equation in (15) gives
\[
 (1-h)\delta=t(E)-\lambda S(M_0)_k+[Q(E+\delta e)]_k+u_3+u_{\mathrm{pol}},
\tag{18}
\]
where the integral remainder \(u_3\) uses (17) and \(u_{\mathrm{pol}}=-\lambda\{S(Z)-S(M_0)\}_k\). The second equation and the first equation in (15) also give the exact identity
\[
 \widehat M_{it}-M_{0,k}=\delta+\lambda S(Z)_k.
\tag{19}
\]
At linear order, (18)--(19) imply
\[
 \delta_1=\frac{t(E)-\lambda S(M_0)_k}{1-h},
 \qquad
 \widehat M_{it}-M_{0,k}
 =\frac{t(E)}{1-h}-\frac{\lambda hS(M_0)_k}{1-h}+\cdots .
\tag{20}
\]
Thus the apparent term \(-\lambda S(M_0)_k/(1-h)\) cancels against the \(+\lambda S(Z)_k\) in (19); only the leverage-sized polar term remains. By (5)--(6), \(|S(M_0)_k|\le C\mu r/n\), so its size is at most \(C\lambda(\mu r/n)^2\). This is the claimed order-\(\lambda\) cancellation.

The established complete-tangent lemma identifies
\[
 \frac{t(E)}{1-h}=\ell_{it}(R_{it}\epsilon)
 =\sum_{j\in C(t)}a_{ij,t}\epsilon_{jt}
  +\sum_{s\in S}b_{t,s}\epsilon_{is}
  -\sum_{j\in C(t),s\in S}a_{ij,t}b_{t,s}\epsilon_{js}.
\tag{21}
\]
In particular, the third summand in (21) is a differential term and cannot be moved into a remainder.

Let \(Z_1=E+\ell_{it}(R_{it}\epsilon)e\). Replacing \(\delta\) by its first-order noise part in the quadratic term of (18), and multiplying by \((1-h)^{-1}\), yields exactly
\[
 \frac{[Q(Z_1)]_k}{1-h}
 =q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)
\tag{22}
\]
by \(\mathrm{def:quadratic\mbox{-}drift}\). The residual from replacing \(\delta\) by its first-order part is \(r^{(\mathrm{res})}_{it}\); the integral in (17) defines \(r^{(3)}_{it}\); and all terms containing \(\lambda\) after the cancellation (20), including derivatives of \(S\), define \(r^{(\mathrm{pol})}_{it}\). Equations (16)--(17), the bounded inverse from the active-resolvent lemma, and the rowwise leverage insertions show that these definitions are uniform over the target set. Combining (18)--(22) proves the displayed expansion and the asserted derivative bounds.
